items.title: The Fock-space convention dictionary for finite type-A quantum modules
items.statement:
Throughout this pair the **source parameter** of the Fock-space literature is
written $s$ and the **library parameter** of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] is written $t$; the
dictionary below sets $t=s^{-1}$.

Let $I$ be a nonempty consecutive set of simple-root indices and put $I^+=I\cup(I+1)$, the coordinate alphabet. On a finite coordinate interval $J=[k,r]\subseteq I^+$ the roots have indices $[k,r-1]$, the coordinate weight lattice is $\bigoplus_{a=k}^r\mathbb Z\delta_a$, $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$ and $h_a=e_a-e_{a+1}$. The full central coordinate is retained. The source algebra $U_s$ has toral generators $D_a^{\pm1}$ for $a\in J$ and root generators $E_a,F_a$ for $k\le a<r$, acting on natural vectors $v_b$, $b\in J$, by

$$D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b,\qquad E_av_b=\delta_{a+1,b}\,v_a,\qquad F_av_b=\delta_{a,b}\,v_{a+1},$$

$$\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1},\qquad \Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a .$$

The library parameter $t$ is identified with $s^{-1}$; the **semilinear Hopf
dictionary** is the coefficient map $t\mapsto s^{-1}$ together with the
generator assignment

$$E_a\longmapsto E_a,\qquad F_a\longmapsto F_a,\qquad K_h\longmapsto D_{-h},$$

where the $E_a,F_a$ on the source side are the *divided* generators of the
source normalization and on the library side those of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] (the assignments agree on the
undivided generators $E_a=E_a^{(1)}$, $F_a=F_a^{(1)}$, and divided powers are
carried to divided powers because the quantum integers are invariant under
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
Root-label weights are preserved, while toral numerical eigenvalues use the
reciprocal parameter: on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the library generator
$K_h$ acts by $t^{\mu(h)}=s^{-\mu(h)}$, which is the action of $D_{-h}$ because
$(-h)(\mu)=-\mu(h)$.

The **bar involution** sends $s\mapsto s^{-1}$, fixes $E_a$ and $F_a$ and
inverts each $D_a$; the corresponding library operation is the involution with
$t\mapsto t^{-1}$, $E_a\mapsto E_a$, $F_a\mapsto F_a$ and
$K_h\mapsto K_h^{-1}$ of [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]
and [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]].

The **natural highest weight** attached to an interval $[k,r]$ is
$\delta_k=\varepsilon_k$ (equivalently the highest weight reached by the
leading coordinate vector $v_k$), its **dual highest weight** is
$-\delta_r$, and the **fundamental wedge weight** is
$\delta_k+\delta_{k+1}+\cdots+\delta_m$ for $k\le m\le r$. Every fundamental
factor carries its own highest-vector-normalized bar, integral lattice and
divided-string crystal charts ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]);
its internal antisymmetrizer embedding is primitive and integral but is *not*
asserted to be based in the library's raw lower $q_0$ chart. Infinite intervals
are defined by the compatible system of their finite subintervals, and
[[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]] with
[[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]] supplies
the library integrable modules used on each finite interval.

The source Fock families $L,T,P$ and the library form-dual upper family
([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]) will
be compared below through their actual forms; they are never identified by
their names.

## Definition

their names.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The type-$A$ root datum with full coordinate weight lattice, a finite interval $[k,r]\subseteq I^+$, the source generators $D_a,E_a,F_a$ with the displayed action and comultiplication, and the library algebra with its generators $E_a,F_a,K_h$ and parameter $t$.

[F1] Library presentation and toral action ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]): $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$, $K_0=1$, $K_hE_aK_h^{-1}=q^{\langle\alpha_a,h\rangle}E_a$, $K_hF_aK_h^{-1}=q^{-\langle\alpha_a,h\rangle}F_a$, and on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the element $K_h$ acts by $q^{\mu(h)}$; the $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra is generated by the $E_a,F_a,K_h$.

[F2] Quantum integers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]): $[m]_q=(q^m-q^{-m})/(q-q^{-1})$ is invariant under $q\mapsto q^{-1}$; the divided power is $x^{(m)}=x^m/[m]_{q_a}!$.

[F3] Library form and bar ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]], [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]): the bar involution is the semilinear endomorphism with $t\mapsto t^{-1}$ fixing the divided generators and inverting $K_h$; integrable highest-weight modules, their normalized highest vectors, bars and lattices are available on finite intervals.

[F4] Existence and uniqueness of integrable highest-weight modules ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]) on the finite-interval subdatum.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** Check the dictionary on generators and relations and conclude it is a well-defined semilinear Hopf identification on each finite interval.

1.1 **Toral relations.** Under $t\mapsto s^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto D_{-h}$, the library relation $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ becomes $D_{-(h+h')}=D_{-h}D_{-h'}$, and $K_0=1$ becomes $D_0=1$; these are the source toral relations. Toral elements commute in both presentations, so $\varphi$ is well defined on the toral subalgebra $\mathbb Q(t)[P^\vee]\to\mathbb Q(s)[\mathbb Z J]$. [F1, algebra]

1.2 **Mixed relations.** The library relation $K_hE_aK_h^{-1}=t^{\langle\alpha_a,h\rangle}E_a$ becomes, after $t\mapsto s^{-1}$, $D_{-h}E_aD_{-h}^{-1}=s^{-\langle\alpha_a,h\rangle}E_a$, and interchanging $h$ and $-h$ this is the source relation $D_{h'}E_aD_{h'}^{-1}=s^{\langle\alpha_a,h'\rangle}E_a$; the $F_a$-relation is the sign-reversed mirror. This matches the displayed action $D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b$ because $\langle\alpha_b,e_a\rangle=\delta_{ab}-\delta_{a,b+1}$; pairing with $h_a=e_a-e_{a+1}$ gives the type-$A$ Cartan matrix. [F1, algebra]

1.3 **The $E$-$F$ commutator.** The library relation $E_aF_b-F_bE_a=\delta_{ab}(K_a-K_a^{-1})/(t_a-t_a^{-1})$ maps to $\delta_{ab}(D_{-a}-D_a)/(s^{-1}_a-s_a)$ where $D_{\pm a}:=D_{\pm d_a h_a}$; both numerator and denominator change sign under the substitution, so the fraction is unchanged and equals the source relation $\delta_{ab}(D_a-D_a^{-1})/(s_a-s_a^{-1})$ after relabelling. No divided generator is modified, as asserted. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.4 **Serre relations.** The Gaussian binomials and the divided powers $E_a^{(m)}=E_a^m/[m]_{q_a}!$ are unchanged as elements under $q_a\mapsto q_a^{-1}$ by [F2]; hence each positive and negative quantum Serre element of the library presentation maps to the corresponding source Serre element, since only the divided powers and the binomial coefficients occur. [F2, algebra]

1.5 **Comultiplication.** Since $K_a$ maps to $D_{-h_a}=D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}$, its inverse maps to $D_{h_a}=D_aD_{a+1}^{-1}$. Thus the library formulas map to $\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1}$ and $\Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a$, exactly the source coproduct. The counit and antipode agree on these generators and hence on the generated algebra. [F1, algebra]

1.6 **Bar involution.** On the source side bar fixes $E_a,F_a$ and inverts $D_a$, hence it sends $D_{-h}\mapsto D_h=D_{-h}^{-1}$; on the library side bar fixes the divided generators and inverts $K_h$. Under the dictionary the two involutions intertwine, and both conjugate the parameter. Consequently bar commutes with the dictionary on the generating set and hence on the generated algebra. [F3, algebra]

1.7 **Weights and labels.** A weight vector of weight $\mu=\sum_a m_a\varepsilon_a$ is an eigenvector of $K_h$ with eigenvalue $t^{\mu(h)}=s^{-\mu(h)}$, which equals the eigenvalue of $D_{-h}$; hence root-label weights are preserved while the toral eigenvalues use the reciprocal parameter, as asserted. In particular $\delta_k=\varepsilon_k$ and $-\delta_r$ are genuine coordinate characters, and the fundamental wedge carries $\delta_k+\cdots+\delta_m$; the central coordinate $\delta_k+\cdots+\delta_r$ is retained. [F1, algebra]

2.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1-1.6 show that the generator assignment preserves every family of defining relations and the Hopf operations on each finite interval, so it extends uniquely to a semilinear Hopf-algebra map $\varphi:U_t\to U_s$ with $t\mapsto s^{-1}$, and symmetrically for the inverse; it is an isomorphism on the subalgebra generated by the finitely many $D_a^{\pm1},E_a,F_a$ with coordinate indices $k\le a\le r$ and root indices $k\le a<r$. Infinite intervals are covered by the compatible finite subintervals, and the library integrable modules and lattices of [F3], [F4] are transported by $\varphi$ on each of them. The comparison of the Fock families through their actual forms, not their names, is carried out in the following items. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 1.5, step 1.6, step 1.7] ∎

items.title: The higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module
items.statement:
Work with the type-$A$ coordinate lattice and the dictionary of
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]];
weights are written in the coordinates $\delta_a=\varepsilon_a$.

Fix a set $I$ of consecutive residues (for the finite box model
$I=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-2\}$ and $I^+=I\cup(I+1)=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-1\}$; $I$ may be
unbounded below or above), a positive **level** $l$, and
$$\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+,\qquad m_1\ge m_2\ge\cdots\ge m_l,$$
where $m_j\in I^+$ and, if $I$ has lower endpoint $k$, $\Lambda_m=\sum_{k\le a\le m}\delta_a$. When $I$ is unbounded below, $\Lambda_m$ is the ground semi-infinite fundamental weight with the finite-coordinate-difference interpretation below. For $I$ bounded below put
$n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in column $j$ and $n=\sum_j n_j$; for $I$ unbounded
below use semi-infinite columns with a common finite tail below, as explained
after the weight definition.

The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is
$$F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_2})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l}),$$
the tensor product of the fundamental modules of the dictionary item. When $I$
is bounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the fundamental integrable highest
weight module of highest weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ in the library algebra. When
$I$ is unbounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge
$\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with $V$ the natural module for the locally finite
type-$A$ algebra on $I$; its basis is the set of normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$ with $i_1>i_2>\cdots$ and the tail
$i_k=m_j+1-k$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ — the columns
$1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$, with rows indexed by $I^+$ — with entries in
$I^+$; it is **column-strict** if in each column the entries strictly increase
from bottom to top and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and
**standard** if in addition the entries weakly increase from left to right in
each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, respectively $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$,
for the sets of column-strict, respectively standard $\Lambda$-tableaux, and
$A_\Lambda$ for the **ground-state tableau** with row $i$ filled entirely
with $i$.

For $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ the **column monomial** is
$$M_A:=\left(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots\right)\otimes\cdots\otimes\left(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots\right),$$
with each wedge normally ordered (the entries strictly decrease from top to
bottom inside a column), and
$$\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)},\qquad \mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A),\qquad \mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$$
for $\alpha\in Q^+$. When a column is semi-infinite, the displayed sum means
its ground fundamental weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ plus the finite sum of the
coordinate differences $\delta_{A(i,j)}-\delta_i$ over the finitely many
positions where $A$ differs from the ground state, evaluated on each
finite-support coroot or torus input; no divergent infinite coordinate sum is
asserted.

The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is defined by $A\le B$ iff
$\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and
$\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$
in the dominance order of [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]] for every
$j<l$; then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$
in columns $i<j$. The column reading of a tableau (list the columns from left
to right, each column read top to bottom) gives the passage to partitions and
to the Young-diagram conventions of
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]; the removable- and
addable-node notation of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]
is used for the box moves of a tableau.

The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is called the **vacuum vector**. Weight
bookkeeping, the uniqueness of the monomial of weight $\Lambda$ and the
bijectivity of the column reading are verified below; the column-monomial theorem records the full integral tensor-basis statement. The well-definedness verification here constructs each fundamental factor explicitly without treating a citation to integrability as a wedge-basis theorem.
items.strategy:
**Given:** The coordinate lattice and dictionary of [[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]], a level $l$ and a dominant weight $\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}$ with $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$; the sets $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda,\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ with the ground tableau $A_\Lambda$, the monomials $M_A$, the weights $\mathrm{wt}_j$ and $\mathrm{wt}$, and the Bruhat order of the Definition.

[F1] Dictionary and coordinate weights ([[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]): the weight lattice is $\bigoplus_{a\in I^+}\mathbb Z\delta_a$ with the full central coordinate, the natural highest weight of the fundamental factor is $\delta_k$, the dual highest weight is $-\delta_r$, and the fundamental wedge carries $\delta_k+\cdots+\delta_m$.

[F2] Partitions and dominance ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]], [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]], [[lem-conjugation-reverses-dominance]]): dominance $\unrhd$ on partitions of a fixed integer is the termwise dominance of prefix sums, and conjugation reverses it.

[F3] Tableau conventions ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]], [[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]], [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]): standard and semistandard tableaux, shapes and removable/addable nodes in the Young-diagram normalization.

[F4] The dictionary supplies the natural representation and its Hopf action, and the existence and uniqueness of its integrable highest-weight quotients. The elementary ordered-wedge construction is proved in step 1.1, not imported from the definition of integrability.

## Verification

1.1 **Elementary fundamental modules.** On a finite coordinate interval $[k,r]$ let $W_n$ have vectors $w_S$ indexed by $n$-element subsets $S$. Put $D_aw_S=s^{\mathbf1_{a\in S}}w_S$, and let $E_a$ replace $a+1\in S$ by $a\notin S$, while $F_a$ makes the opposite replacement, both with coefficient one and zero otherwise. The toral relations follow from the changed coordinate; $[E_a,F_a]$ is $1$, $-1$ or zero on the three possible $a,a+1$ occupation patterns, exactly the toral fraction. Different-root mixed commutators vanish by the same replacement test. Distant replacements commute; for adjacent roots $E_a^2=F_a^2=0$ and $E_aE_bE_a=F_aF_bF_a=0$, since the last replacement encounters the already occupied endpoint. These are the adjacent Serre relations. Distinct subset weights are separated by the toral operators, and successive raising replacements take any subset to $\{k,\ldots,k+n-1\}$; lowering generates every subset from it. Thus this module is integrable and irreducible, of highest weight $\Lambda_{k+n-1}$, and is the fundamental module in the dictionary. The ordered wedge symbol denotes this model; the primitive antisymmetrizer realizes it integrally, without any assertion that the raw tensor lower chart makes that embedding based. [F1, F4, construct, algebra]

2.1 **Root rows and physical rows.** In column $j$ the root row runs from $k$ to $m_j$, whereas its physical height is $n_j=m_j+1-k$. The monomial therefore starts at $A(m_j,j)$ and descends through $A(m_j-1,j),\ldots,A(k,j)$. Its entries are strictly decreasing in that order and define a nonzero $w_S$ from step 1.1. Physical row $h$ means root row $k+h-1$; its row length is $\#\{j:n_j\ge h\}$. Hence the ordinary partition diagram is the conjugate of $(n_1,\ldots,n_l)$, not of the possibly negative multicharge. Column reading is a bijection to tuples of strictly decreasing entry blocks of these fixed lengths; the standard row inequalities are the corresponding semistandard inequalities. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **Weights and the vacuum.** The toral formula in step 1.1 gives precisely $\mathrm{wt}_j(A)$ and their sum on the tensor monomial. The ground column is $\{k,\ldots,m_j\}$, with weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$. Every other column weight differs from its ground by a nonzero element of the positive root cone: repeatedly raise its subset to the initial segment, decreasing its weight difference by a simple root at every step. The tensor top weight can therefore occur only when every factor is its ground vector. Its weight space is one-dimensional, spanned by $v_\Lambda$. This argument uses the explicit finite factor construction, not a yet unproved global-basis inclusion. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

3.2 **The prefix order.** Use root dominance: a weight difference is nonnegative when it is a nonnegative integral combination of $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$; on fixed-total-coordinate weights this agrees with the usual coordinate prefix criterion. Reflexivity and transitivity are immediate; equality of every factor-prefix weight forces equality of each column subset, hence of the column-strict tableaux, proving antisymmetry. If $A$ has $a$ in an earlier column $i$ and $b>a$ in a later column $j$, and $B$ swaps them, the prefix difference $\mathrm{wt}_{\le u}(A)-\mathrm{wt}_{\le u}(B)$ is $\delta_a-\delta_b=\sum_{v=a}^{b-1}\alpha_v$ for $i\le u<j$ and zero otherwise. Thus $A<B$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Infinite intervals.** Every fixed tableau differs from its ground only finitely many times. Choose an actual finite lower cut below all those changes, never an undefined $\inf I$ when $I$ is unbounded below, and a finite upper cut above all displayed entries and charges. Appending a common ground tail gives the same action of every root generator in the common subinterval: its adjacent occupation pattern is unchanged. The finite weight differences and all prefix comparisons are unchanged. The compatible union constructs the semi-infinite factors and tensor module; each fixed finite-support calculation is one of the finite computations above. Highest-weight uniqueness and the ground argument remain valid on those finite cuts. [F1, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2]

5.1 **Conclusion.** The module, tableau labels, column monomials, root-coordinate weights and prefix order are well defined, and the vacuum is the unique normalized highest-weight tensor monomial. Ordinary physical partitions use the shifted column heights. All admitted consecutive intervals and multicharges are retained; no raw-chart basedness or additional choice is asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: The column monomial basis of the higher-level Fock module
items.statement:
Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]] with
source parameter $s$.

(1) For a finite interval $[k,r]$, the normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{i_d}$, $i_1>\cdots>i_d$, $i_a\in[k,r]$, form an
integral basis of the fundamental wedge $\Lambda^d V$, where the wedge is the
antisymmetrized tensor word with coefficients $(-s)^{\ell(w)}$ over the
symmetric group; the span is primitive over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$. This does
not assert that the antisymmetrizer embedding into the raw tensor power is based
in the library's lower $q_0$ chart.

(2) The column monomials $M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, form a basis of the
higher-level Fock module $F(\Lambda)$ on every finite cut, with the weights
$\mathrm{wt}(A)$ of the Definition.

(3) Let a finite interval $[k,r]\subseteq I^+$ be a **cut** containing all
entries of a given monomial (upper cut), and $k-1<k$ a further lower residue;
the **lower-cut embedding** $\iota_k$ appends the common bottom entry $k-1$ to
each of the $l$ columns, $\iota_k(M_A)=M_{A\sqcup(k-1)^l}$. The embeddings are
injective, compatible with the monomial action, and their compatible direct
limit over shrinking lower cuts and growing upper cuts is the full bounded or
semi-infinite Fock module of the Definition.

(4) Every generator acts by finitely many box moves and shifts weight spaces;
each fixed-weight space of $F(\Lambda)$ is finite dimensional. A merely
lower-bounded infinite interval need not give finite-dimensional fundamental
factors; all finite-Cartan statements are applied on finite cuts.
items.strategy:
**Given:** A finite cut $[k,r]$ of the consecutive residue set $I^+$, a level $l$ and dominant weight $\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}$ with $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$, the fundamental wedge $\Lambda^dV$ of the natural module with basis $v_i$, and the column monomials $M_A$ of [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]].

[F1] Dictionary and Fock conventions ([[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]], [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]): the source generators act by $D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b$, $E_av_b=\delta_{a+1,b}v_a$, $F_av_b=\delta_{a,b}v_{a+1}$; the fundamental factors are the integrable highest weight modules $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ with highest weight vectors the ground wedges; weights are computed by $\mathrm{wt}(A)$.

[F2] Integrability and tensor products ([[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]], [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]): integrable highest weight modules exist, are generated from their highest weight vectors by divided lowering powers, and tensor products of integrable modules are integrable.

[F3] Crystal and lattice suppliers ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]], [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]], [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]]): crystal bases, tensor rules and highest-weight decompositions in the library normalization.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The ordered-word lattice for one fundamental factor.** Define the exterior quotient by $v_a\otimes v_a=0$ and $v_b\otimes v_a=-s^{-1}v_a\otimes v_b$ for $b>a$. Thus sorting an ascending adjacent pair into descending order contributes $-s$, not a positive scalar. The coproduct sends a repeated-letter relation under $E_a$ or $F_a$ to the corresponding signed adjacent relation; on distinct letters the same two-term computation preserves that relation. Hence the quotient is a module. Sorting distinct letters has scalar $(-s)^{\ell(w)}$; commutation and braid moves preserve the number of inversions, and repeated-letter words vanish. The quotient therefore has one independent ordered generator for each distinct-letter orbit. [F1, algebra]

2.1 **The integral basis and primitive antisymmetrizer.** The quotient sorting relations have Laurent-unit coefficients and disjoint permutation orbits, giving a free ordered-word lattice. In the tensor lattice the alternating word of a descending tuple is the sum over permutations with coefficients $(-s)^{\ell(w)}$, with ordered coefficient one. Different tuples have disjoint supports; their span is a direct summand by taking the ordered coefficients and is therefore primitive. A coproduct replacement on the alternating sum cancels if it creates a repeated letter, and otherwise gives the alternating word of the replaced tuple with coefficient one; the two adjacent terms are exactly the cancellation checked in step 1.1. Thus sending an ordered quotient vector to its alternating word is an integral module isomorphism onto this span. No raw tensor-chart basedness is inferred. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **The wedge is the fundamental module with its own lattice, bar and crystal.** On ordered wedges the generators act by replacing a single entry: $E_av_b=\delta_{a+1,b}v_a$ and $F_av_b=\delta_{a,b}v_{a+1}$ on letters, extended multiplicatively to a wedge; an attempted replacement producing a repeated letter gives $0$. The top wedge is annihilated by all $E_a$ and is the highest weight vector; divided lowering powers reach every ordered wedge, so the wedge is generated as the integrable highest weight module $V(\Lambda_m)$ with highest weight $\Lambda_m=\sum$ of its ground letters, and the ordered-wedge lattice is its divided-power lattice with the induced bar involution and crystal chart. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 **The tensor basis.** The tensor product of fundamental factors has as integral basis the tensor products of their ordered-wedge bases, i.e. precisely the column monomials $M_A$ with one wedge per column; by [F2] the tensor product is integrable and its weight is the sum of the factor weights, which is $\mathrm{wt}(A)$ as computed in [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. This proves (1) and (2) on a finite cut. [F1, F2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 **The lower-cut embeddings.** Appending the same entry $k-1$ below every column defines a linear map on the span of monomials; since the appended letters are smaller than every letter of the cut, the image is again a span of ordered wedges, so $\iota_k$ is injective and intertwines the common-root generator action: the appended letter is never moved by a generator whose residue lies in the cut, for the common root subalgebra. No assertion says the new boundary generator acts by zero: it may move the appended letter when the next letter is absent. The embeddings for decreasing cuts are compatible, and every semi-infinite tableau differs from the ground state in finitely many positions, hence belongs to the image of some lower cut and to some upper cut. [F1, step 4.1, construct]

6.1 **Direct limit and finiteness.** The compatible system of the maps of step 5.1 with upper cuts containing all entries of the monomials gives the full Fock module as a direct limit; generators act by finitely many box moves because each generator replaces one letter in one factor, hence shifts the weight by a root and changes only finitely many entries; a fixed weight fixes the multiset difference from the common ground tail, so only finitely many tableaux occur and the weight space is finite dimensional. All finite-Cartan suppliers of [F2], [F3] are applied on the finite cuts, where every module involved is finite dimensional; no finite-dimensionality is claimed for fundamental factors on a merely lower-bounded infinite interval. [F1, F2, F3, step 5.1] ∎

items.title: The tensor-product bar on the Fock module and its truncation compatibility
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]], with
source parameter $s$ and the ordered column-monomial basis
$\{M_A:A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda\}$ of
[[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]].

(1) On every finite interval the Fock module carries an **ordinary compatible
bar** $\psi$, the tensor-product quasi-$R$ bar built from the factors' own
normalized bars on the finite-product based integrable modules of
[[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]].
It is involutive (semilinear with $s\mapsto s^{-1}$) and independent of the
parenthesization of the tensor factors.

(2) It is **triangular** on the monomial basis:
$$\psi M_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]\,M_B$$
in the Bruhat order of the Definition; it fixes each ordered fundamental wedge,
and it preserves the integral monomial lattice
$\bigoplus_A\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]M_A$.

(3) Both kinds of truncation commute with $\psi$ and preserve the actual
charts and bases: an upper-cut inclusion of the smaller coordinate alphabet (equivalently the inverse identification on the supported truncation),
and the common-bottom-tail embedding
$\iota_k(M_A)=M_{A\sqcup(k-1)^l}$, satisfy
$\psi\iota_k=\iota_k\psi$ and map bar-fixed/chart vectors to bar-fixed/chart
vectors. Hence $\psi$ induces a well-defined bar on the full direct limit of
[[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]],
including the semi-infinite columns.

Its finite products are used only on actual finite-Cartan based fundamental
factors; no universal two-sided-unbounded tensor theorem and no arbitrary
integral quasi-$R$ action claim is imported.
items.strategy:
**Given:** Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] as specified above.  A finite interval $[k,r]$, its Fock module $F(\Lambda)$ on that cut with ordered column monomials $M_A$, and the reduced finite products of fundamental factors with their own normalized bars and integral lattices.

[F1] Finite-product tensor bars ([[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]], [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]], [[lem-quasi-r-intertwining-determines-the-inverse-and-coproduct-factorizations]], [[lem-quasi-r-divided-power-integrality-on-based-lattices]]): on finite products of based integrable modules, the quasi-$R$ construction defines an involutive tensor bar compatible with the factors' bars, with the inverse and coproduct factorizations determined by the intertwining data, integrality on based lattices controlled by divided powers, and the stated admissible finite-product scope.

[F2] Monomial basis and weights ([[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]], [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]): the ordered wedges and their tensor products form the integral monomial basis; generators act by finitely many box moves, shift weights, and the Bruhat order compares the prefix weights of tableaux.

[F3] Conventions ([[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]): bar fixes the divided generators, inverts $D$, and sends $s\mapsto s^{-1}$; the fundamental factors are based with their own highest-vector-normalized bars.

[F4] Global bases and balanced triples ([[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]): the finite-interval comparison interfaces for lower global bases and their bar-fixed lifts.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The bar on a finite cut.** On a finite cut take the reduced finite product of the tensor factors $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ and equip each factor with its own normalized bar of [F3]. The finite-product theorem [F1] produces an involutive semilinear bar on the tensor product, compatible with the factor bars; by [F2] the basis of this module is the set of column monomials $M_A$ of the cut. This defines $\psi$ on each finite cut. [F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 **Triangularity.** In the actual positive-first-factor quasi-$R$ convention, every nonconstant term raises the weight in an earlier tensor prefix and lowers the complementary suffix by the same positive root. The prefix-dominance definition therefore puts every resulting label strictly below $A$. The constant term is one, and each factor bar fixes its ordered minuscule wedge vector. The finite-product divided-power integrality makes every coefficient a Laurent integer, proving the displayed triangular formula. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 **Involution and parenthesization independence.** Both properties are inherited from the finite-product theorem [F1]: applying the tensor bar twice returns the original element because each factor bar is involutive and the quasi-$R$ twist is inverted by the inverse factorization; reassociating the tensor factors replaces the product of quasi-$R$ twists by its twisted product, and the intertwining relations [F1] identify the corresponding bars. [F1, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 **Integral monomial lattice.** Since $\psi M_A$ differs from $M_A$ by integral combinations of lower monomials (step 2.1), the $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$-span of the $M_A$ is stable under $\psi$; the same holds for $\psi^{-1}=\psi$. [step 2.1]

3.2 **Upper cuts.** Consider a larger upper coordinate interval and a tensor supported on the old alphabet. A positive operator in an earlier prefix can only replace a letter $a+1$ by $a$, never create a letter above the old upper bound. Every quasi-$R$ term involving a new upper-boundary root therefore kills that prefix. Terms supported on old roots agree with their old-cut terms, and the fundamental bars fix the same ordered vectors. Reassociate successive prefixes using step 2.2. Thus the larger bar restricts to the old bar, rather than relying on an incorrect letter-replacement description of the factor bars. [F1, F2, step 2.2]

4.1 **Common lower tails.** After appending $k-1$ to every factor, each earlier tensor prefix has every wedge occupied at $k-1$. Any positive-root word involving the new boundary must apply $E_{k-1}$ at some stage. Earlier positive replacements on old roots preserve that occupancy; $E_{k-1}$ either encounters no $k$ or attempts to create a duplicate $k-1$, and kills each factor, hence the prefix. The entire quasi-$R$ correction involving the new boundary is zero. The old-root toral weights of the appended tail are zero, so all surviving old-root terms and factor bars agree with the old calculation. This proves $\psi\iota_k=\iota_k\psi$ on finite products. Common-root string operators and integral lattices are preserved; uniqueness of balanced lifts therefore preserves the actual charts and bases. No assertion says all new generators vanish on the image. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.2, step 3.2]

5.1 **The direct limit.** Every vector of the full Fock module lies in the image of some finite double cut, and every calculation in the expansion of $\psi$ is finite and stabilizes in a cut containing the residue and the input and output supports by steps 3.1, 3.2. Hence the compatible family of bars defines a bar on the direct limit, still involutive and triangular, and it fixes each ordered fundamental wedge. No infinite series is taken. [F1, F2, step 2.2, step 3.2, step 4.1]

6.1 **Conclusion.** On every finite cut the Fock module has the ordinary compatible bar $\psi$ of (1)-(2); the upper-cut and common-tail embeddings commute with it by (3), so it descends to the full bounded or semi-infinite module. All uses are confined to actual finite-Cartan based fundamental factors; neither a universal two-sided-unbounded tensor-bar theorem nor an arbitrary integral quasi-$R$ action is asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

items.title: The dual-canonical, canonical and quasi-canonical Fock bases
items.statement: Use source $s$ and the ordinary Fock bar $\psi$. The monomial basis is $M_A$. The SOURCE dual-canonical family is the $\psi$-fixed $L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\mathbb Z[s]M_B$; the canonical family is the $\psi$-fixed $T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]M_B$. Define $M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)L_A$, $L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)M_A$, and $P_A=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)M_B$, so $M_A=\sum_Bp_{A,B}(-s)P_B$. Both $L,T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not. Reverse-factor monomials $\widetilde M_A$ and their bar/bases use reverse-column reading, with $\widetilde L_A$ supported on $B>A$. Define the SOURCE sesquilinear form by $\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$ (antilinear first argument), and the bilinear reverse-factor form by $C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}$. Thus labelled monomial Gram matrices are the inverse ordinary-bar matrix, not identity. Transition duality gives $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$ and $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$. Rectification identifies the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. All four families are Laurent-integral bases and commute with cuts. On the highest constituent the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library polarization differ by an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison below; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.
items.strategy: Triangular bar correction in each finite weight set gives both complementary coefficient charts, their unitriangular inverses and integral bases; cuts preserve the same equations. If B is the ordinary-bar matrix, the defining forms have Gram B^-1. Substitute the two coefficient matrices and apply coefficient conjugation in the first sesquilinear argument to obtain the three displayed delta identities; their domains are original and reverse-factor modules as stated. Raw reverse E/F matrices are transposes of the coefficient-conjugate original F/E matrices, so the bar in the second argument gives the bilinear EF-swap contravariance with torus fixed. The sesquilinear adjoint is the source semilinear tau, not this bilinear anti-involution. Finite column signatures and row-insertion/reverse-insertion preserve the selected cancelling signs and show the two ground components and rectification dictionary; the highest-constituent theorem supplies the complete based inclusion and projection proof. Both T and L fixedness follows from their definitions and may not be contradicted later in the Definition. All of this uses the SOURCE chart normalization; actual8 upper polarization and adjoint bar are compared only after the explicit weight rescaling.

items.title: Parabolic semi-regular duality and the reverse-column label map
items.statement: For a lower-bounded Fock tableau shape, set n_j=m_j+1−inf(I), n=sum n_j and lambda_A,j=a_j+j−1 from its finite column reading. These data define the genuine finite integral parabolic CENTRAL SUMMANDS by the structural category of15; no connectedness is assumed. Assume AC. For the reversed-block standard parabolic $\bar p\subset gl_n$, grade simple Levi roots by0 and outside roots by1, so $g_0=\bar l$, $g_{<0}=\bar u^-$ and $\gamma=2\rho_g-2\rho_{\bar l}$ is a Levi character. There is the explicit semi-regular $U(g)$-bimodule $S_{\bar u,\gamma}=U(\bar u^-)^\#\otimes U(\bar p)$, with the two PBW module identifications. Tensor/Hom give inverse exact equivalences on finite-rank graded free/cofree $U(\bar u^-)$ objects. Restricted contragredient dual and $c(X)=-w_0X^tw_0$ give an exact CONTRAVARIANT equivalence $\Psi$ from finite generalized-standard flags for $\bar p$ to those for $p$. The Levi highest-weight map is $\lambda_{\bar A}\mapsto-w_{\bar J}\lambda_{\bar A}-2\rho_{\bar u}$, then $-w_0$; in reverse/original column readings it gives $a_i+i-1$, so $\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A)$. BGG restricted duality $D$ gives the COVARIANT equivalence $F=D\Psi$ from opposite standard flags to target costandard flags, with $F(\bar\Delta(A))=\nabla(A)$. It preserves the corresponding central blocks and reverses the label order. These are exact filtered-category assertions, not equivalences on all objects of category O and not the unchanged underived full-longest Borel twisting functor.
items.strategy: Highest-weight/Levi admissibility and shifted-multiset character follow directly from these readings and the actual15 generic category, independently of the later connected-block Definition. Use the outside-root grading and finite-Levi PBW slices from15. The character identity gamma([X,Y])=tr_l(adX adY) follows by Levi invariance, checking outside simple e_alpha against f_alpha with the root/sl2 trace calculation; other weights give0. Construct right action via N# tensor_N U and left action via Hom_B(U,C_gamma tensor B). For H in l, H(f tensor1)=−(f adH)tensor1+f tensor(H+gamma(H)); for X in g1 decompose nX=Xn+sum H_i H_i^X(n)+F_X(n), giving X(f tensor1)=f tensorX+sum(fH_i^X)tensor(H_i+gamma(H_i))+(fF_X)tensor1. Commutation with right g−1 reduces to the displayed trace identity, and generation by g0,g±1 proves bimodule commutation. The left PBW map is triangular for positive Levi-radical degree followed by Levi PBW degree: leading f tensor b and strictly lower corrections prove surjectivity and injectivity by finite induction, avoiding the source's false finite-dimensional degree-zero comparison. The adjoint unit/counit reduce to graded free/cofree evaluation and End_N(N#)=N^op, so no completion is hidden. On an induced finite Levi simple E, the dual top space is C_−gamma tensor E*, hence the stated standard transport; induction restricts both functors to finite flags. Ungraded transfer uses zeta eigenvalue classes moduloZ and restricted weight duals. In a target column of lengthr and offsetb the reverse source offset isb'=n−b−r; w0w_Jbar preserves within-column position and 2w0rho_ubar=b−b'. Thus transformed component a_i+(b'+k−1)+(b−b')=a_i+i−1. This proves the exact label and scalar central shift. D then changes variance and standards to costandards. The source free/cofree and flag hypotheses are checked here, not presumed for arbitrary O.

items.title: Standard- and costandard-filtered objects and tilting objects
items.statement:
Assume the inherited AC for the finite genuine parabolic CENTRAL SUMMANDS and their highest-weight ideals; no connectedness is assumed. $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(
abla)$ denote finite standard/costandard flags; a tilting object has both. These exact categories are closed under sums and summands, multiplicities are independent, $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_A,
abla_B)=\delta_{AB}\mathbb C$ and all positive Ext vanish. The finite highest-weight criteria are $\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,
abla_A)=0\  orall A\}$ and its dual, equivalently using all positive Ext. Restricted duality exchanges the two flags. The normalized indecomposable tilting of label A has $\Delta_A$ once at the bottom and all other standard labels STRICTLY SMALLER in the tableau order; A is the unique maximal support label, not a minimal one. In a lower ideal containing A this tilting is unchanged.
items.strategy: Consume the ACTUAL generalized-standard trace/Hom/Ext1/BGG proof of15, not the ordinary Verma lemma restricted without proof. Standard projective kernels and dual injective cokernels have flags with strictly ordered support; dimension shifting gives higher Ext vanishing. For the homological criterion, Ext1(N,∇)=0 gives all higher Ext by those finite costandard coresolutions. Remove a maximal label e from the basic finite block algebra; the canonical trace gives heredity ideal Ae⊗eA with Ae=Δ_e,eAe=C. For B=A/AeA every injective B-object is costandard-filtered with the lower labels, so all positive Ext_A(N,I_B) vanish. A projective resolution and tensor/Hom adjunction then force Tor_j^A(B,N)=0 (injective B-objects detect its homology). Hence 0→Ae⊗eN→N→B⊗N→0; the quotient has the same vanishing overB and induction gives a standard flag. Duality proves the other criterion. Idempotent trace peeling preserves flags under summands. The tilting classification theorem applies these criteria and proves the maximal-label uniqueness; no false Δ→∇ injection or min-label hypothesis is used.

items.title: Type-A tableau central summands are single linkage blocks
items.statement: Assume AC. For the Fock shape $n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_l$ (the original nonincreasing-charge hypothesis) and any admitted integral entry multiset, the genuine $gl_n$ parabolic central summand labelled by its strict-column tableaux is a SINGLE linkage block. The same holds for its reverse-column/reversed-Levi counterpart. This includes repeated-entry singular ambient characters. The proof uses actual indecomposable generalized standards and locally constructed tiltings: adjacent-column positive exclusive-pair canonical coefficients specialize to1, so those labels lie in a common actual linkage block; these edges connect the whole fixed-margin binary tableau fiber. No future higher-Schur/cyclotomic-centre theorem is imported.
items.strategy: Do not presume connectedness. Work in the actual15 finite highest-weight central summand, possibly a product, and use the earlier parabolic standard-flag equivalence Psi. Put X(B)=Psi(Pbar(B)). Its standard flag has labelB once at the bottom and onlyA<B otherwise, by opposite BGG/order reversal. Projectivity makes Ext1(Delta,X)=0, so the independently proved generic criterion makes X tilting. Both X andDX have the same maximal normalized flag; extending the bottom inclusion both ways and finite local-End/Fitting proves selfduality. Thus (X(B):M(A))=[barM(A):barL(B)]. To identify these coefficients with SOURCE T at1, use the direct tensor/wedge matrix bridge: sortingw is shortestRIGHT in the ENTRY stabilizer and d=w^-1 shortestLEFT. Pure tensor Hecke generator action and the reverse-position complementary-chart pairing (sourceB1§4, with reciprocal parameter) identify tensor d(1) with spherical P_{d(C)w0,d(A)w0}(1), exactly15singular ordinary multiplicities. Finite Levi Weyl cancellation gives the signed column-permutation expansion of genuine generalized standards. Source-positive wedge embedding sends its L to tensorL by ordinary-bar and triangular uniqueness, hence the same signed matrix is the actual parabolic d. Apply this also in reverse columns. The typed C(tildeL,T)=delta gives (X(B):M(A)) equal to the coefficient of M(A) in source T_B at1. All this concerns central SUMMANDS, so invokes neither connectedDefinition nor later16Ringel/tilting theorem. Now independently construct the two-column canonical coefficient: CWZ0409016§4.3–4.4 defines disjoint positive pairs (left exclusive b>right exclusive a), chosen by increasing b−a distance and discarding previously used endpoints. With q=t=s^-1 its normal wedge action/coproduct equals this library/source dictionary. The source3case Procedure4.11 reduces to a typical tuple with no positive pairs; its monomial is ordinary-bar fixed since every positive-first quasi-R correction would need an exclusive b>a pair. In the reduction steps the explicit wedge Chevalley formulas give either K_f alone or K_f+qK_swapped. Each Chevalley generator is bar fixed. The recursion terminates lexicographically in the number of matched pairs and the sum of their distances: losing a pair lowers the first measure, and retaining the pairs moves only the selected endpoint inward. The source Lem4.14 induction therefore gives a bar-fixed qZ[q]-triangular vector; uniqueness identifies the canonical vector. Its3cases prove U_f=sum_{Sigma subset greedy positivepairs}q^{#Sigma}K_{fSigma}. Distinct subsets change distinct exclusive entries, so each single-pair coefficient is EXACTLYq. This is a complete two-factor proof, not a super-duality conjecture. For adjacent columns in a larger tensor, endpoints agreeing outside those columns have identical outer prefix weights. Every tableau in their Bruhat interval has those same outer prefix weights. Parenthesize with the pair as one factor: a positive transfer across an outer boundary would strictly change a prefix weight and cannot be cancelled by further positive transfers. Thus the interval bar matrix, and by triangular correction its canonical coefficient, equals the two-column matrix. At1 a greedy-pair edge gives (X(B):M(A))=1; indecomposable X(B) has both simple heads as composition factors, so A,B lie in the SAME actual original block. Opposite BGG gives [barM(A):barL(B)]=1, and barM(A) also has headbarL(A), so the same edge connects the opposite blocks. To connect all labels, identify a tableau with the0/1 incidence matrix of which entry values occur in each column; row margins are entry multiplicities and column margins are n_j. Two such matrices differ by alternating cycles in their bipartite symmetric difference. A long cycle splits by a chord: if the chord is0 flip the smaller4cycle first, otherwise flip the complementary shorter cycle first; induction flips the entire cycle while restoring the chord. Hence arbitrary valid2x2 switches connect the fiber. Reduce a switch between nonadjacent columnsS,U through the next intermediate columnT. IfT has onlya or onlyb, two switches with shorter column distance suffice. IfT contains botha,b, choose c inS\T: it exists because |S|>=|T| andT\S containsb. Perform c↔b betweenS,T, a↔b betweenT,U, thena↔c betweenS,T, restoringT and making the desired S/U switch. IfT contains neither, choosec inT\U (exists |T|>=|U| andU\T containsb), and use c↔b betweenT,U, a↔b betweenS,T, thena↔c betweenT,U. Induct distance; all switches remain binary and preserve margins. Sorted ORIGINAL heights justify precisely these cardinal comparisons. Finally any adjacent-column switch lies in a fixed two-column union/intersection fiber. Repeatedly swapping a greedy positive pair strictly lowers its inversion order until the unique configuration with all left-exclusive values below right-exclusive values; hence all such fibers connect through the already-proved coefficient1 edges. Combining the paths proves original and opposite linkage connectedness. This supplies the full promised singleblock result without merely asserting a shuffle graph or importing future17/18 centre-surjectivity.

items.statement: Assume AC and $I$ bounded below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite (the upper end of $I$ may remain unbounded). Let classical $g=gl_n(\mathbb C)$ and the standard parabolic have Levi $gl_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus gl_{n_l}$. For the column reading $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $A$, set $\lambda_A=\sum_j(a_j+j-1)\varepsilon_j$ and let $L(A)$ be its simple highest module. Strict columns make this Levi-dominant, so the simple and the induced generalized standard $M(A)$ belong to genuine $O^p$. Use the published HALF-SUM convention $\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$. Then $\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+(n-1)/2$, so their $gl_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$; this labels the central character, together with the displayed scalar $gl_n$ centre. The Fock weight $\sum\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ belongs to the DIFFERENT $gl_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that multiset, not a literal gl_n highest weight. The corresponding finite parabolic central blocks $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ have labels $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$, projectives $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with BGG and restricted duality from15. Their simple/standard bases and numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central characters. The direct sum over these characters is $O^\Lambda$. Opposite blocks use reversed Levi order and reverse-column reading, with the corresponding reversed label order.

items.statement:
For $I$ bounded below use the actual finite classical tableau-block dictionary (including repeated entries). Fix the right place action $(a w)_i=a_{w(i)}$. Let $w_A$ be shortest with $a(A)w_A$ weakly increasing, and let $K$ be the Young stabilizer of that sorted multiset. Then $w_A$ is shortest RIGHT modulo $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ shortest LEFT, and
$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2}).$$
This is the ANTISPHERICAL/sign family for the ENTRY stabilizer, in the left convention after inversion, with Hecke variable $v=s$; the library QUANTUM parameter is instead $t=s^{-1}$. It has support $A\le B$ and diagonal1; $d$ is its inverse coefficient matrix through $p(-s)$. The COLUMN Levi subgroup $J$ is generally different from $K$. Assuming AC, the genuine parabolic block composition matrix is
$$[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_{C\sim_{\rm col}B}(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1).$$
This uses singular ordinary SPHERICAL coefficients for the entry stabilizer inside finite Levi cancellation, so covers mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi blocks. It does not identify a singular category with genuine parabolic O or identify the two polynomial families by an opposite convention.
items.strategy: Check the tensor Hecke generators directly on tuple monomials, with reciprocal sourceB1 parameter; sorting identifies trivial induction for K and the opposite triangular chart is sign induction. Project ordinary KL vectors to the sign quotient. Simultaneous inversion gives p_{w_Az,w_B}=p_{z^-1d(A),d(B)}, so the15 alternating-sum/triangular uniqueness theorem gives the displayed FULL polynomial identity, not a sample or q=1 family test. The source-positive-s wedge antisymembedding has ordered leading coefficient1, positive-degree within-column corrections and compatible ordinary bar (highest-factor intertwining and quasi-R naturality). Expanding a source L_A gives the ambient tensor L_{a(A)} by positive-chart uniqueness; this embedding is not asserted library-lower based. At1,15 singular ordinary multiplicities give [M(a):L(c)]=P_{w_a w0,w_cw0}(1)=P_{d(a)w0,d(c)w0}(1), by inversion plus longest conjugation. Finite Levi Weyl characters/PBW give ch M(B)=sum_C (−1)^ell(B,C)ch ordinaryM(C). Comparing with the same signed exterior monomial expansion in the tensor L basis proves d_AB(1) equals the displayed mixed parabolic matrix, using character injectivity. Thus regular and singular ambient cases are both closed locally without Koszul or double-coset category equivalence.

items.title: Standard tableau monomials form a basis of the highest weight Fock submodule
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], with source
parameter $s$, monomial basis $M_A$, ordinary bar $\psi$, source
dual-canonical family $L_A$, canonical family $T_A$, and the source forms
$\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$.

The highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$ generates the multiplicity-one constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$, and there is its normalized module projection
$\pi:F(\Lambda)\to V(\Lambda)$.

(1) The vectors $S_A:=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of
$V(\Lambda)$, and $D_A:=\pi L_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ form the
**source dual-canonical basis** of $V(\Lambda)$.

(2) What vanishes is $\pi L_A$ for $A$ not standard; $\pi M_A$ need not vanish
for nonstandard $A$. The integral kernel of $\pi$ is the saturated direct
summand with basis the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and
$\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ has the actual basis $D_A$ (also $S_A$ on
$\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$), the source upper/costandard lattice. For every $B$,
$$\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$$
which gives the explicit straightening of nonstandard projected monomials.

(3) All bases and maps commute with upper cuts and common-tail embeddings, so
the assertions hold in the full direct limit. The relation of the source
$D_A$ to the library form-dual upper family
([[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]) is the explicit weight
rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison, not an unqualified
identification.
items.strategy:
**Given:** Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] as specified above.  A finite cut of $F(\Lambda)$ with its monomial basis, ordinary bar $\psi$, source families $L,T$, forms $\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$, the highest constituent $V(\Lambda)$ with its normalized highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$, and the library based-module machinery.

[F1] Fock bases and forms ([[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], [[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]], [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]): monomial basis and its weights; triangular charts $d,p$; $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$, $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$, $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; rectification identifies $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; cuts commute with all four families.

[F2] Based modules and global bases ([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]], [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]], [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]], [[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]], [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]): the normalized integrable highest module is ordinary simple and maps universally to an integrable cyclic highest module; finite tensor charts have the stated crystal rule; the contravariant form and its normalized highest constituent; existence, bar invariance and uniqueness of the lower global basis; bar lattices and crystal lattices.

[F3] Conventions ([[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]): source/library parameter dictionary, divided powers, bars and lattices.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The normalized highest inclusion.** The explicitly constructed fundamental factors make the ground tensor integrable and give it the unique top weight $\Lambda$. The universal highest-module map from the actual existence-and-uniqueness theorem sends the normalized highest vector to this ground tensor and has nonzero image. Ordinary simplicity of that highest module makes the map $j:V(\Lambda)\to F(\Lambda)$ injective. A module injection preserves each highest kernel and the unique divided-string decomposition, hence commutes with the intrinsic lower string shifts. It also sends divided-power generators to the actual integral tensor lattice. The normalized projection will be constructed by the finite nondegenerate pairing below, rather than assumed from a general semisimplicity assertion. Its uniqueness follows from the one-dimensional top weight: a nonzero map to the simple highest module is surjective, hence cannot vanish on the top weight. [F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 **The actual balanced tensor chart.** Let $L_0^{\rm ten}$ and $\Psi L_0^{\rm ten}$ be the actual two charts of the finite-product theorem, not the raw tensor-word chart. The normalized ground tensor is a nonzero ground crystal residue. Every generator of $L_0(\Lambda)$ is a divided-string word on its highest vector; the naturality established in step 1.1 and the actual tensor crystal rule put its image in $L_0^{\rm ten}$ with the corresponding nonzero ground-component residue, with nonvanishing ensured by the partial-inverse rule. Divided-power generation gives $jV_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)\subseteq F_{\mathcal A}$. Both bar composites agree on the highest vector and on every bar-fixed divided lowering monomial, so $j\overline{L_0(\Lambda)}\subseteq\Psi L_0^{\rm ten}$. Hence $jG(b)$ is integral, lies in both actual charts, is bar fixed and has the required residue. Balanced uniqueness identifies it with the corrected tensor global vector. Since $t=s^{-1}$, this library zero chart is the source infinity chart: the original factor order yields $T_A$ on $\mathrm{Rev}$, and the reverse-factor order yields $\widetilde T_A$ on $\mathrm{Std}$. This proves based inclusion rather than assuming every module map is based. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **The ground components.** On a strict column the crystal signature rule has $+$ for entry $i$ and $-$ for entry $i+1$ with simultaneous occurrences cancelling; concatenating down-column words, cancelling $-+$ pairs, the rightmost surviving $+$ and leftmost surviving $-$ determine the source upper operators. Semistandard rows are stable under this rule: a changed entry violating a row inequality has an equal neighbouring entry which is either a later surviving $+$, an earlier surviving $-$ or its cancelling mate, and column strictness forces the last matching in the same row strip. The only highest tableau of the closed set is the ground state: the rightmost column is consecutive ground, and inducting to the left, rows overlapping the already-ground right columns are forced to be ground while a gap above the overlap produces an unmatched minus; repeated raising decreases the sum of entries, bounded below on a finite interval. Thus the reverse-factor lower ground component, equivalently the source original-order upper signature component, is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; the original-order lower component is the reverse-standard set from step 2.1. [F1, F2, step 2.1]

4.1 **Rectification.** Reversing the tensor order gives the reverse reading of the same signature rule; aligning column tops by the prescribed vertical shifts makes the reverse-standard inequalities stable, and the explicit row-insertion rectification (bumping the smallest larger letter, with the elementary Knuth interchanges preserving the cancelling signs) is a weight-preserving crystal isomorphism between the original lower ground component and the reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, with inverse reverse insertion. This is the label dictionary of [F1]. [F1, step 3.1]

5.1 **The projection.** Define $\pi$ by $C_0(v,\pi y)=C(j_{\mathrm{reverse}}v,y)$, where $j_{\mathrm{reverse}}$ is the based reverse-factor highest inclusion. The required highest form is constructed from the actual library polarization $B_8$: at weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ put $C_0=s^{a(\alpha)}B_8$, $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$. Its nondegeneracy and highest value one follow from $B_8$. The translated adjoint is $\sigma(F_i)=sK_i^{-1}E_i$, $K_i=D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$. For input weight $\mu$ this contributes $s^{1-\mu(h_i)}$, canceled by $a(\alpha+\alpha_i)-a(\alpha)=\mu(h_i)-1$. Thus $C_0(F_ix,y)=C_0(x,E_i y)$, and similarly $C_0(E_ix,y)=C_0(x,F_i y)$; toral operators remain self-adjoint. This constructs, rather than assumes, the normalized nondegenerate $\mathcal E\mathcal F$-contravariant form. Here is the needed typed contravariance locally. Let $B_0$ be the coefficient dot pairing of reversed and original tensor words, and write $\Psi=\Theta\overline{(\cdot)}_0$ on a finite product, with $\overline{(\cdot)}_0$ the factorwise coefficient bar. Since $\Psi M_B=\Theta M_B$, the normalization $C(\widetilde M_A,\Psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}$ gives $C(x,y)=B_0(x,\Theta^{-1}y)$. On each minuscule factor the matrices of $E_i$ and $F_i$ are transposes. Reversing the factors in the explicit coproduct therefore gives $B_0(E_i x,z)=B_0(x,\overline\Delta(F_i)z)$, $B_0(F_i x,z)=B_0(x,\overline\Delta(E_i)z)$, while toral $D_a$ is self-adjoint. The finite quasi-$R$ intertwiner satisfies $\Theta\overline\Delta(u)=\Delta(\overline u)\Theta$; for $E_i,F_i$ their bars equal themselves. Substitution proves $C(E_i x,y)=C(x,F_i y)$, $C(F_i x,y)=C(x,E_i y)$ and $C(D_a x,y)=C(x,D_a y)$, first on two factors and then by coproduct association on each finite product. The required complementary delta pairing can also be checked here. The paired-root Casimir terms of the finite quasi-$R$ expansion, under factor reversal and the minuscule $E/F$ transpose, give $\Theta_{\mathrm{reverse}}^{\mathsf T}=\overline\Theta^{-1}$; the inverse/factorization identities extend this from two factors to every finite product. Consequently $C$ commutes with both bars in the sense $C(\widetilde\Psi x,\Psi y)=\overline{C(x,y)}$. Since $L_B=\Theta\overline{L_B}_0$, one has $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=B_0(\widetilde T_A,\overline{L_B}_0)$. The two coefficient families on the right have coefficients in $\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$, with constant matrix the identity and every off-diagonal term in $s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$. Their value is bar fixed by the preceding identity, hence belongs to $\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\cap\mathbb Z[s]=\mathbb Z$, forcing $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$. The triangular bar-fixed families used here are obtained locally in finite weight spaces: at each lower label, involutivity makes the residual coefficient $r(s)$ satisfy $r(s)+r(s^{-1})=0$; its positive-power part, or negative-power part, gives the unique required correction, and induction on the finite lower ideal constructs the complementary charts. Thus this use requires neither an unproved Gram identity nor a presumed based embedding. These identities are over $\mathbb Q(s)$; any stated complex coefficient conjugation is restored on scalar extension. Thus the normalized highest form $C_0$ has precisely the required $E/F$ adjunction and toral symmetry, and $\pi$ is $U$-linear; its highest coefficient is $1$, so its composite with the original highest inclusion is the identity on the simple highest module. It is therefore a genuine normalized projection, and its uniqueness is the top-weight argument of step 1.1. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 4.1]

6.1 **Vanishing and the dual-canonical basis.** Since $j_{\mathrm{reverse}}$ sends the lower global basis to $\widetilde T_A$ with $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, the delta pairing $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$ of [F1] gives $\pi L_B=0$ for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, while for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ the vectors $D_A=\pi L_A$ form the $C_0$-dual basis of the constituent. This proves the vanishing statement (2) and that the $D_A$ are the source dual-canonical basis. [F1, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 **Straightening and the $S$-basis.** Expanding $M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ by the triangular chart of [F1] and applying $\pi$ gives $\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$ the restriction to $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ of a unitriangular matrix with diagonal $1$; hence the projected monomials $S_A=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of the constituent and the displayed formula is the explicit straightening of every projected monomial, standard or not. No projected-monomial vanishing is claimed. [F1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 **The integral kernel and the source upper lattice.** By step 6.1 the kernel of $\pi$ is spanned by the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; being spanned by a subset of a basis it is a saturated direct summand of the integral Fock lattice. The image $\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ is spanned by the $D_A$, hence is the source upper/costandard lattice; it is not identified with the lower divided-power lattice by an $A$-unit Gram determinant, since the relevant monomial Gram matrices are the inverse ordinary-bar matrix rather than the identity. [F1, step 6.1, step 7.1]

9.1 **Cuts and the direct limit.** All constructions and all coefficients of steps 1.1-8.1 are stable under the upper-cut and common-tail embeddings by the declared truncation compatibility theorem, and every vector lies in some finite double cut; the normalized highest maps are unique, so the maps agree on overlaps. The compatible direct limit gives the full bounded or semi-infinite assertion, and the comparison with the library form-dual upper family is the explicit weight rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 8.1]

10.1 **Conclusion.** The highest Fock constituent $V(\Lambda)$ has the standard monomial basis $S_A$ and the source dual-canonical basis $D_A=[\pi L_A]$ over $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, with the explicit straightening formula and the saturated integral kernel off $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; the library comparison uses the weight rescaling only. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 8.1, step 9.1] ∎

items.statement: Assume AC and finite classical $gl_n$ tableau blocks. Define $f_i$ by tensoring with its natural module and projecting onto the entry-multiset character with one $i$ replaced by $i+1$; define $e_i$ by the dual natural module and the reverse character change. On their direct sum these are exact and biadjoint, preserve projectives/injectives and commute with the restricted transpose duality. Equivalently $f_i$ is the generalized eigencomponent $i$ of tensor Casimir and $e_i$ is the generalized eigencomponent $-n-i$ on the dual tensor product. They are special residue translations, not automatically ordinary regular-wall translations. The Fock root label shifts by $\pm\alpha_i$; that label is not the classical gl_n highest weight.
items.strategy: General finite-tensor/block-projection biadjunction is the ACTUAL general clause of the published translation supplier, applied to V and V*, not a sequence of unproved regular wall crossings. Tensor finite modules preserves genuine parabolic local finiteness, and exact block projection/Levi Hom gives the same adjunction inside O^p. Restricted transpose duality fixes both finite natural modules with their respective forms, so each residue functor commutes with it. Highest-weight scalar Casimir calculation is supplied by the earlier local Casimir lemma before any head/socle consumer. All block labels are the explicit shifted-coordinate multisets.

items.title: Residue Casimir operators and local affine-Hecke actions
items.statement: Assume AC and work with finite $n$ classical $gl_n$ category O, distinct from the Fock algebra $gl_{I^+}$. Tensor Casimir $x_j$ on the jth natural factor (including all preceding factors) and adjacent place swaps $T_j$ on $M\otimes V^{\otimes r}$ satisfy the degenerate affine-Hecke relations: commuting $x_j$, symmetric-group braid/quadratic relations, $T_jx_j-x_{j+1}T_j=-1$ and commuting distant generators. They restrict naturally to repeated residue functors $f_i^r$, where $x_j-i$ is locally nilpotent; dual actions are biadjoint mates on $e_i^r$. Finite Levi tensor decomposition and exact PBW induction give multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags for the entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. The standard-class map $[\Delta(A)]\mapsto M_A$ gives the full integral Fock K0 action, its Chevalley/Serre relations and local integrability; each root's biadjoint functors therefore give a positive, locally finite $sl_2$ action on the simple-class basis. The ground-state class generates the highest constituent, not generally the entire tensor Fock module.
items.strategy: The natural tensor Casimir is sum E_ab tensor E_ba, and x_j adds the place transpositions with earlier natural factors. Matrix-unit multiplication proves x commutation and T_jx_jT_j=x_{j+1}−T_j, hence the listed relations, with braid and distant commutation immediate on places. For highest weight lambda_j=a_j+j−1, c(lambda)=sum lambda_j(lambda_j+n+1−2j), c(V)=n; the eigenvalue on the lambda+epsilon_j flag factor is (c(lambda+epsilon_j)−c(lambda)−n)/2=lambda_j+1−j=a_j. On lambda−epsilon_j in tensor V* it is −a_j−n+1; an entry i+1 therefore gives −n−i. Exact generalized eigenspaces select precisely the moves. Tensor identity plus finite Levi complete reducibility produces each valid column move once; projected invalid/repeated-column moves disappear. Standard and simple K0 bases and character injectivity were proved in15, so the standard-class map is an actual isomorphism and the induced generators are the explicit tensor/wedge action. Checking on this basis proves Chevalley and Serre relations, including the integral divided powers. Each residue root is locally finite because the fixed finite boxes have only two relevant entries and repeated replacements terminate. Biadjunction, finite length and positivity in the simple basis make class vanishing equivalent to functor vanishing, satisfying every weak-sl2 hypothesis without a forward reference to the later combined action theorem. Restrict x to the chosen generalized eigenfunctor; nilpotence follows on finite flags, hence on finite length. Define the dual x/T by mates, which preserves the relations and both adjunctions.

items.title: The local affine-Hecke socle argument for residue translations
items.statement: Assume AC and the preceding positive biadjoint residue $sl_2$/local degenerate affine-Hecke action. At a coincident eigenvalue the completed affine-Hecke algebra on r steps is $Mat_{r!}$ over the completed symmetric polynomial centre. The first-i image in its central fibre is $Mat_{i!}(Z_{i,r})$, where $Z_{i,r}=\mathbb C[c_1,\ldots,c_i]/(h_{r-i+1},\ldots,h_r)$ is a finite local complete-intersection Frobenius ring of dimension $\binom ri$ and one-dimensional socle. Divided residue functors and the complementary-idempotent restriction have the corresponding simple head/socle. Consequently $e_iL(A)$ and $f_iL(A)$ are either0 or self-dual indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled $\tilde e_iA$ and $\tilde f_iA$, respectively. Vanishing is exactly absence of that crystal edge. This retains the complete residue-translation crystal claim, not only its K0 action.
items.strategy: Use polynomial representation T_j=s_j−partial_j, partial_j=(1−s_j)/(x_j−x_{j+1}); PBW follows by ordered spanning and leading permutation independence after localization. At the coincident completion, partial_j=(x_j−x_{j+1}+1)^−1(1−T_j), with LEFT inverse. Polynomial multiplication and longest divided difference give the relative perfect trace; reduction is the actual coinvariant Frobenius pairing, and complete-local Nakayama gives every matrix unit. The trivial/sign symmetric-group idempotents have fibre rank1: divided-difference terms lower degree and the diagonal character is the regular coinvariant character; idempotent splitting and Nakayama lift rank1. Partial elimination of remaining elementary coefficients gives the displayed h-relations. Their only common zero is0, since vanishing of i consecutive h's and their recurrence makes the reciprocal elementary series polynomial, hence constant. Nullstellensatz makes the quotient finite; polynomial Cohen–Macaulayness and the actual system-of-parameters theorem give regularity, globally by homogeneous localization. Koszul Hilbert series yields dimension binomial(r,i); the variable and h Koszul resolutions compute a unique socle in degree i(r−i). Thus no Grassmannian/Poincare theorem is imported. The ordered partial ring is free of rank i! over this centre and has dimension r!/(r−i)!, by successive monic distinguished-root equations. PBW group cosets and this basis prove the restriction freeness; the complementary idempotent removes (r−i)! multiplicity and leaves the indecomposable projective over Mat_{i!}(Z), with simple head/socle. These are the full algebraic steps of CR3.2–3.3/3.6. In the positive simple-class basis the sl2 string-height filtration is stable; biadjunction prevents a socle/head summand of E^jS from having lower maximal string height than S. At an extremal simple FS=0, E^(r)S is a single opposite-extremal simple by finite sl2 string theory/positivity. The Hecke action on E^rS has multiplicity module K_r; complementary restriction forces the socle/head of E^(j)S simple, since no maximal-height summand is killed by E^(r−j). Dimension comparison gives binomial(r,j) leading multiplicity and smaller-height other factors. For a general S take an extremal quotient of F^(h_minus)S and use adjunction to embed S in its divided translate; the opposite extremal translate is a sum of one simple, and the adjoint Hom into its simple socle bounds its multiplicity by1. This proves CR5.20 without importing it as a black box. Source Fock L is the balanced SOURCE upper-chart family. Kashiwara93§5.1 proves kernels of powers spanned by the global vectors with bounded epsilon (apply the maximal string power and balanced injectivity); §5.2 finite sl2 highest-string filtration is balanced by isolating a maximal constituent and annihilator test, whose remainder lies in the zero triple intersection. Thus in each associated string fG=[phi]G(tilde f) and eG=[epsilon]G(tilde e), and all other constituents have smaller corresponding height. The actual upper/lower string definitions in§3, the two source-positive coefficient charts and the typed reverse pairing verify these hypotheses; this is not the library8 adjoint-bar family by fiat. The full source5.3.1 proof uses the upper divided-string expansion and kernel-spanning induction to lift that leading term. At1, comparing with the preceding categorical unique maximal-height factors gives precisely the stated tableau labels. Commuting restricted duality makes head and socle equal and gives self-duality; one simple socle forces indecomposability.

items.title: The residue translation functors give the integrable Fock-space action
items.statement: Assume AC. The exact residue functors on genuine finite-n parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags given by valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. Their K0 operators are the full integrable $gl_{I^+}$ Fock Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the standard basis. For each simple, a residue translate vanishes exactly when its corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual indecomposable with simple equal head/socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$ or $L(\tilde e_iA)$. The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the ground-state class, with $M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one highest constituent. No action on labels alone proves the K0 relations or head/socle statement.
items.strategy: The earlier Casimir supplier proves actual flags, the standard-class isomorphism, relations and local integrability BEFORE the head lemma, so there is no circular dependence on this combined theorem. The local affine-Hecke helper proves the complete categorical extremal-string/simple-socle argument and matches labels by the actually read source-upper Chevalley leading-term proof. Apply it with E=f_i,F=e_i (and the swapped root orientation), then use restricted duality. For the ground multiset the column-strict admitted label is unique: successive strict entries at least their row ground values, with that minimal total weight forcing equality. The15 highest-weight/character bases therefore make its standard simple and projective. All quantum global/form claims have their own explicit later dictionary; this is the ungraded categorical result.

items.statement: Assume AC and $I$ bounded below. The standard-class map $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$ identifies the direct-sum K0 of genuine tableau parabolic blocks with the full integral Fock module, with matching multiset degrees and residue Chevalley action of $gl_{I^+}$. For every projective $P$ and finite-length $N$, $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ at $s=1$. In particular $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; no false standard/simple orthogonality $\langle M_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$ is asserted. The projective, simple and tilting basis identifications are proved separately below.
