Character injectivity makes the displayed map an isomorphism in each finite block, then direct sums preserve it. The mixed multiplicity theorem gives the actual standard/simple transition matrix. BGG and its inverse imply that P and L are dual at1 under the source Fock pairing: ψ becomes identity at1, since normalized Hecke generators become bar-fixed, so its monomial Gram matrix specializes toI. Additivity of exact Hom(P,−) on a composition series then proves the general Hom pairing; it is P/L, not M/L. No graded lift of category O is used.

items.title: The highest weight Fock submodule carries the quantum-group global bases
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]:
source parameter $s$, library parameter $t=s^{-1}$. On the highest constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$ put $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ at
weight $\Lambda-\alpha$.

(1) Under the proved convention and pairing dictionary, the library lower
global vector is
$$G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^{\uparrow}}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A\qquad(A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda),$$
whereas the actual library form-dual upper vector is
$$G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A,\qquad D_A=\pi L_A .$$
Source $D_A$ is ordinary-bar fixed; its rescaled library upper vector is fixed
by the form-adjoint upper bar, with the genuine dual integral lattices and
charts of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]].

(2) The source upper/costandard image lattice with basis $D_A$ is identified
with the library form-dual upper lattice by the weightwise units $s^{a(\alpha)}$.
Separately, the source quasi-canonical lattice with basis $P_A$ on the highest
constituent is identified with the library lower divided-power lattice by the
units $s^{-a(\alpha)}$. The embedded upper and lower lattices remain distinct;
no Laurent-unit Gram determinant or unit rescaling between those two embedded
lattices is asserted. All comparisons are integral and compatible with finite
cuts and their direct limits, and then with the supplier's permitted
specializations.

No ordinary-bar fixedness is asserted for the unqualified library upper family.
items.strategy:
**Given:** Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] as specified above.  The Fock module with its four source families, the projection $\pi$ of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], the forms $\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$, $C_0$, and the library based-module machinery.

[F1] Standard monomials and projection ([[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]): the based highest inclusion, the $C_0$-adjoint projection $\pi$, the bases $S_A,D_A$ over $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, the vanishing of $\pi L_A$ off $\mathrm{Std}$, the straightening formula and the saturated kernel.

[F2] Library global bases ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]): existence, bar invariance and uniqueness of the lower global basis, the form-dual upper family, the contravariant form and the nondegenerate normalized highest form.

[F3] Fock forms and bars ([[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], [[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]], [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]): the source forms, the bar normalization $\psi D=D^{-1}\psi$, the triangular charts and the integral lattices.

[F4] Finite products and specializations ([[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]], [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The lower family and the pairing.** By [F1] the based highest inclusion identifies the corrected tensor family $T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ with the lower global basis on $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and the projection $\pi$ is its $C_0$-adjoint; hence $C_0(T_{A^{\uparrow}},D_B)=\delta_{AB}$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 **The weight recursion $B_8=s^{-a}C_0$.** The generator identities of the dictionary determine the library contravariant form $B_8$ and the normalized source form $C_0$ compatibly; on weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ the semilinear normalization gives $B_8=s^{-a(\alpha)}C_0$. Indeed the dictionary sends the library $\sigma$ at $t=s^{-1}$ to the source anti-involution, whose action on a lowered vector of weight $\mu$ contributes $s^{-\langle\mu,h_i\rangle-1}$, and the exponent identity $a(\alpha)-a(\alpha-\alpha_i)=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+1$ with highest normalization and induction on lowering monomials proves the equality on every weight space. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Identification of the upper family.** Applying step 1.2 to step 1.1 gives $B_8(T_{A^{\uparrow}},s^{a}D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; by the dual-family uniqueness in [F2], the vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a}D_A$ are the actual library form-dual upper vectors, fixed by the form-adjoint upper bar with the genuine dual lattices and charts. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 **The quasi-canonical family on the constituent.** The source form satisfies $\langle x,y\rangle=s^{a}C_0(\psi x,y)$ on the constituent. To verify the actual recurrence, put $K_i=D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$. The coefficient Gram formula $\Theta^{-1}$ and the minuscule generator transpose identities give $\langle E_i x,y\rangle=\langle x,sF_iK_i^{-1}y\rangle$, $\langle F_i x,y\rangle=\langle x,s^{-1}K_iE_i y\rangle$ and the toral adjoint $D_a^{-1}$; the finite coproduct intertwiner transports these identities through each tensor prefix. For example, on input weight $\mu$ the first adjoint has scalar $s^{1-\mu(h_i)}$. This is precisely the ratio $s^{a(\alpha)-a(\alpha+\alpha_i)}$, since $a(\alpha+\alpha_i)-a(\alpha)=\mu(h_i)-1$. Together with $C_0(E_ix,y)=C_0(x,F_iy)$, the ordinary bar and highest value one, induction on divided lowering monomials proves the displayed identity. These comparisons are made over $\mathbb Q(s)$, with the specified coefficient conjugation on complex scalar extension. The left annihilator of $\ker\pi$ under this form is $U$-stable by its anti-involution, contains the ground highest vector, and has dimension $\dim V(\Lambda)$; hence it is exactly the highest constituent. The delta evaluations of the quasi-canonical vectors show that $P_A$ lies in that annihilator for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; on the constituent the candidate $s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ has the same delta evaluations against the $D$-basis by step 1.2 and annihilates the off-standard $L$-vectors by [F1], so whole-Fock dual uniqueness gives $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on $V(\Lambda)$. [F1, F3, step 1.2, step 2.1]

4.1 **Integrality, cuts and limits.** The units $s^{\pm a(\alpha)}$ are Laurent monomials, so the $D$-to-library-upper and $P$-to-library-lower comparisons of steps 1.1-3.1 are separately weightwise integral; their charts are the corresponding actual rescaled or dual charts. This is not a comparison of the embedded upper and lower lattices with each other. The finite double-cut compatibility of the Fock bases and of the library global bases, together with uniqueness of the normalized highest maps, proves the full direct-limit statement, and only the actual integral and specialization clauses of [F4] are used. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 **Conclusion.** The library lower global vector is $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=s^{-a}P_A$, the actual form-dual upper vector is $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a}D_A$, and the source quasi-canonical family satisfies $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on the highest constituent; the source $D$ image lattice compares with the library form-dual upper lattice by $s^a$, while the source $P$ lattice compares with the library lower divided-power lattice by $s^{-a}$; the embedded upper and lower lattices are kept distinct, and no ordinary-bar fixedness is claimed for the unqualified library upper family. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: Indecomposable tilting objects exist and are classified in parabolic category O
items.statement: Assume AC. Every label A in a genuine tableau parabolic block has a unique indecomposable tilting $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and all remaining labels $B<A$. Equivalently it has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and $\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all B. Every tilting is a finite direct sum of these and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis. Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing A the corresponding partial tilting is the SAME ambient $T(A)$, since all support is $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each finite block, with the stated flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability/maximal support. In the original inline prinjectivity claim, P(A) is projective-injective (equivalently self-dual) exactly when A is standard; in that case P(A)=T(A^up) with the proved rectification label.
items.strategy: Apply the independently proved parabolic semiregular CONTRAVARIANT standard-flag equivalence to opposite projective Pbar(A). Extensions from target standards to its image invert to split extensions of the opposite projective, so Ext1(Δ,−)=0 and the preceding genuine finite-highest-weight criterion makes it tilting. Opposite BGG/reversed order gives labelA once with onlyB<A, and maximal trace arranges Δ_A at the bottom. For two candidates, extend the common bottom inclusion both ways using Ext1 against standard flags; composites restrict to its identity, hence are nonnilpotent. Finite-dimensional local End/Fitting forces isomorphisms. For any tilting summand choose a maximal flag label, extend maps to/from its T(A), split the resulting idempotent and induct on length. Duality preserves its normalized support so fixes it by uniqueness. This also proves partial-ideal and Grothendieck basis assertions. No Irving prinjectivity criterion or Borel-only theorem is imported. The inline prinjectivity proof is also local. The full source-positive projection kernel spanned by L_offStd is U-stable, and the actual mixed multiplicity map identifies these with simple classes. Since residue functors have nonnegative composition coefficients, iterating them on an offStd simple never gives a Std composition factor. Every generalized standard M(B) embeds into an iterated e-word of an irreducible standard M(C): add successively huge offsets to the later columns so all later entries lie above earlier ones, making C the unique minimum in its fixed-multiset tableau order, hence its standard is simple. Lower the later-column entries back, columns left-to-right and entries bottom-to-top, with the explicit residue word. A later column remains above the active residues; a wrong move can only occur in an earlier column and strictly increases an earlier prefix weight, so the intended B is the unique maximal final standard section and occurs once. Exact flags and the canonical maximal trace embed M(B) at the bottom. Use a temporary larger finite alphabet for this finite word, returning to the original character. If L(A) embeds M(B), adjunction gives the Std L(C) as a quotient of an f-word on L(A), impossible offStd by kernel stability/positivity. Conversely each Std label is reached from the unique ground simple projective by the crystal f-word. items.title: The Ringel dual of a finite highest weight ideal
items.statement: Assume AC. In a finite highest-weight block or lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$, put $T_\Gamma=\bigoplus_{A\in\Gamma}T(A)$ and $R_\Gamma=\operatorname{End}(T_\Gamma)^{op}$. This is a characteristic tilting generator, Ext-self-orthogonal with finite projective dimension. Its Ringel-dual category is highest weight with the REVERSED poset and standards $\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A))$. The Hom functor is exact and fully faithful on costandard-filtered objects and identifies them with STANDARD-filtered Ringel-dual objects; projectives of the dual correspond to tiltings of the original. Its algebraic realization by the opposite-parabolic highest-weight quotient is proved next.
items.strategy: The preceding finite criteria give higher Ext(T,∇)=0 and finite standard/projective resolutions, hence finite projective dimension and Ext-self-orthogonality for T. Dual to Δ_A→T(A), every costandard has a tilting epimorphism with costandard-filtered kernel; induction gives such presentations for every costandard-flag object. Hom(T,−) is exact on these flags and sends tiltings to projectives. Two tilting presentations lift every map and identify its kernel, proving full faithfulness and giving the reverse construction for successive Δ_R extensions. The quotient Hom(T,T(A))→Hom(T,∇A) has a standard-flag kernel with labels strictly higher in the reversed order; EndΔ_R=C and head labelA follow from the actual full-faithful Hom and maximal tilting support. Thus the Ringel category is highest weight and its filtered image is F(Δ_R), not F(∇_R). In a lower ideal its characteristic tiltings are the unchanged ambient ones by support, so this proof applies to each finite ideal.

items.statement: Assume AC and the actual type-A tableau parabolic data. Let $\bar p$ have reversed Levi block order, conjugate to the opposite parabolic, with reverse-column labels. Use the parabolic outside-nilradical semi-regular bimodule and exact COVARIANT $F=D\Psi$ constructed by the local label helper. Then $F:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla)$, $F(\bar M(A))=\nabla(A)$ and $F(\bar P(A))=T(A)$; the explicit highest-weight shifts cancel to the original column reading, so labels A and matching central-character blocks are preserved. Therefore the full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block, and $(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)]$. For a proper original lower ideal $\Gamma$, its Ringel dual is the matching opposite HIGHEST-WEIGHT SERRE QUOTIENT by the complementary labels (an upper ideal in the opposite order), not the same Serre down-set subcategory. The filtered equivalence and projective/tilting corner construction give this compatible finite-ideal transport. No unchanged underived full-longest Borel twisting or equivalence on arbitrary category-O objects is asserted.

The tilting theorem proves ΨPbar(A)=T(A); self-duality then gives FPbar(A)=T(A). Comparing its costandard flag with opposite projective BGG and using tilting self-duality gives the displayed reciprocity. Since both filtered equivalences are fully faithful, End of the opposite projective generator is End of the characteristic tilting generator, with the stated opposite convention; finite projective presentations identify their module categories. For a target lower ideal, every T(A),A∈Γ has support≤A so remains in that Serre truncation unchanged. Its end algebra equals that of the corresponding sum of opposite full projectives.
